Crypto Fee Calculator

Fees are charged on the whole position, twice. Price them before the trade does.

How it is calculated

round trip = 2 × position × fee%  |  monthly = round trip × trades

The gap between maker (resting limit orders) and taker (market orders) fees looks tiny per trade and enormous per year — an active trader on $10k positions can hand the exchange a four-figure sum annually purely for impatience.

Worked example

$10,000 position, 0.055% taker vs 0.02% maker, 40 trades/month: taker costs $440/month, maker $160 — limit orders keep $3,360 a year.

FAQ

Why are maker fees lower?

Resting limit orders provide the liquidity that makes the book usable, so exchanges reward them with lower fees or rebates; market orders consume liquidity and pay for immediacy.

Do fees depend on leverage?

Fees apply to position value (margin times leverage), so raising leverage with the same margin raises the fee bill proportionally.

What other costs exist?

Perpetuals exchange funding every 8 hours, and market orders pay slippage. The break-even and funding-cost calculators price the full round trip.
